doctrine: A schedule of DETECTION READINGS, not a compliance calendar. 'Due' means a reading is due; it never means an obligation is met or unmet. The pack records whether a named method DETECTS a machine-readable mark in a given set of bytes AT A GIVEN TIME. That reading is true as of its date and not before it.
why_a_schedule_exists: The Art 50 marking census of 2026-09-12 carries no detection reading for any generator stack: every detectable slot is UNMEASURED because no sample probe was run. Until a reading is taken, the pack states what a vendor says it does, not what a method can see. And once a reading exists it decays, because a C2PA manifest carries a validity window and IPTC metadata is stripped when a file is re-saved. A detection reading without a date is a claim about no particular moment.

law.pre_existing_systems_basis: Article 111(4) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, as added by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Article 1(39)(b) (OJ L, 24.7.2026; in force 27 July 2026)
law.pre_existing_systems_text: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.
law.reading: Quoted for the reader's own reading. The reading beside it records whether a named method DETECTS a mark in the stated bytes at the stated time. It draws no conclusion about whether the obligation is met.

inputs.note: The census is the input whose bytes this schedule pins. If the pinned digest stops matching, a reading is due whatever the calendar says: the thing being scheduled has changed.

points.why: The census carries no detection reading for any stack: every detectable slot is UNMEASURED because no sample probe was run. This is the first reading, and until it exists the pack states posture rather than detection.
points.measures: For each generator stack on the census, run the named methods against a permitted sample and record DETECTED or NOT DETECTED per slot, with the sample's own sha256 and the time of the run.
points.note: the census carries no detection reading yet; every detectable slot is UNMEASURED

points.why: Article 111(4) gives systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 until 2 December 2026. A reading taken before that date is a baseline that predates the date itself.
points.measures: The first detection reading, re-taken, so that two readings of the same bytes exist either side of the date.
points.note: a reading before the Article 111(4) date, so two readings exist either side of it

points.why: The date Article 111(4) itself names. A reading that does not exist on this date says nothing about this date.
points.measures: A detection reading dated 2026-12-02, per stack, with the method version that produced it.
points.note: a reading dated 2026-12-02, the date Article 111(4) itself names

points.why: The same bytes, one week later. Two readings of one artefact across the date are what show whether detection moved, rather than the artefact moving.
points.measures: A second reading of the same sample bytes as the 2026-12-02 reading, so the two can be compared byte for byte.
points.note: the same bytes one week later, so a change in detection is visible

points.why: A detection reading decays: a C2PA manifest carries a validity window and IPTC metadata is stripped when a file is re-saved. A reading from 2026-12-02 is a statement about 2026-12-02.
points.measures: A detection reading for every stack on the census, with the method version that produced it, three months after the previous one.
points.note: a reading every quarter; a detection reading decays as manifests expire

triggers.rule: A reading is due now if the sha256 of the census file differs from the pinned digest, whatever the calendar says.
triggers.why: The schedule is a schedule FOR a particular input. If the input's bytes changed, the readings taken against the earlier bytes do not describe it.

triggers.rule: A reading is due now if the version of any named detection method differs from the version recorded in the reading it supersedes.
triggers.why: A detection reading is about a method as well as about bytes. A new method version is a different instrument, and the earlier reading is not a reading of it.

limitations: this is a schedule of readings, not a compliance calendar; due means due, not met and not unmet
the census this schedule pins carries no detection reading yet, so every detectable slot is UNMEASURED
DETECTED and NOT DETECTED describe what a named method can read in a given set of bytes at a given time; they say nothing about any other output, method or moment
the C2PA manifest store and IPTC metadata are the only mark kinds this pack reads; no watermark, fingerprint or other kind of mark is read
metadata is often stripped when a file is re-saved, so a NOT DETECTED reading is a fact about those bytes and not about the system that made them
